title: Agent spec struct and a registry holding triage@1 and implement@1, read by nothing

story.i_want_to: one compiled description of each dispatch kind
story.so_that: later stories can move each kind onto it with an equivalence test, and the lists that must agree are held equal by a test

rationale: PRD: a spec is a compiled struct in a code registry, never a tenant row, because its outcomes and effects decide which custody edges a runner message can drive.

acceptance_criteria.description: Loopctl.Agents.Spec defines the fields: id, version, archetype (:judge | :build | :draft), kind, candidates, sweeps, payload, refs, runner, budgets, result, screens, outcomes, effects, rerun, concurrency, prompt ({template_id, version}). Every closed-set field is validated at compile time against its allowed values.
Loopctl.Agents.Registry returns triage@1 (:judge) and implement@1 (:build), transcribing today's behaviour; nothing in lib/ reads it yet.
A spec naming a stage transition outside its archetype's allowed set fails to compile: a :judge or :draft spec can name only control-only edges, and no spec can name a human_only edge.

A registry test binds: registry kinds == RunnerContract.Kinds.all/0 == the dispatch_records kind CHECK; triage@1 outcomes == TriageVerdict outcomes and its @routes; budget keys == DispatchPayload.budget_keys/1; every named transition is in StageMachine.transitions/0.
No per-tenant table and no API: specs change only through code.

test_cases.name: registry agrees with the contract
steps: compare with Kinds.all and the migration CHECK

test_cases.name: illegal edge refused
steps: compile a :judge spec naming a runner-reportable edge
expected_results: CompileError naming the edge and the archetype

test_cases.name: human edge refused
steps: compile any spec naming escalated -> queued human_resolution

technical_notes: Load .claude/skills/chain-of-custody/SKILL.md: outcomes and effects are custody inputs.
Mutation check: drop the archetype edge check, the illegal-edge test must fail.
